question: Which committee adopted the cost of living as the basis for identifying poverty?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Tendulkar Committee**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Tendulkar Committee** adopted the cost of living as the basis for identifying poverty.
 
• This committee was established to review the methodology for poverty estimation in India.
 
• The Tendulkar Committee suggested a shift from the calorie-based norm to a broader measure that includes expenditure on food, education, and health.
 
• Based on its recommendations, the poverty line was redefined to reflect the cost of living in both rural and urban areas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Tendulkar Committee** was constituted in 2005 by the Planning Commission of India.
 
• The committee's report was submitted in 2009 and has been a significant reference point in discussions about poverty in India.
 
• Prior to the Tendulkar Committee, the **Lakdawala Committee** was responsible for poverty estimation, which primarily used calorie intake as the measure.
 
• The change in methodology was aimed at providing a more comprehensive understanding of poverty and improving the targeting of welfare schemes.
